learningObjective: Create and set up blob containers (names, anonymous access) and file shares (protocol, tier, size limit, mounting).
engineer: Container names: 3 to 63 characters; lowercase letters, numbers and hyphens; start with a letter or number; no two hyphens in a row.
Folders in blob storage: a '/' in a blob name only looks like a folder. Real folders exist only with hierarchical namespace.

Anonymous access levels: Private, the default, with no anonymous access; Blob, where anyone with the URL can read a blob; Container, where anyone can read and also list the blobs. Blob and Container only appear if the account allows blob anonymous access.
Blob types: block blobs, for most data; append blobs, for logs (you only add to the end); page blobs, for random reads and writes, such as VHD disks.
Container features: immutability policies (time-based retention, legal hold); metadata; stored access policies.
Standard file shares (on Standard GPv2 accounts): pay as you go, with three tiers: Transaction optimized, Hot and Cool. SMB only. Size limit 5 TiB, or up to 100 TiB with large file shares turned on.
Premium file shares (on FileStorage accounts): you pay for the size you reserve (provisioned). SMB or NFS 4.1. Up to 100 TiB.
Mounting a share: SMB uses TCP port 445. The share's Connect page gives you a ready script (net use on Windows, mount on Linux). If port 445 is blocked, use a private endpoint or VPN.
Azure File Sync: keeps a copy (cache) of the share on your own Windows Servers.
Hierarchical namespace (Data Lake Storage Gen2): containers become file systems, with real folders, POSIX permissions (ACLs) and a dfs endpoint.

example.title: Website images and team shares
body: Marketing serves product images from a container with Blob-level anonymous access. It's in its own storage account, the only one where anonymous access is allowed, and Azure Front Door sits in front.
The finance team's share 'finance' (Hot tier, 2 TiB limit) is mounted as drive Z: on their PCs, through a private endpoint, with identity-based access.

architectureDecisions: Public files get their own account: then anonymous access can stay off everywhere else.
Pick shares by need: premium for low latency or NFS, standard Hot or Cool for ordinary file shares.

misconceptions.myth: Normal blob storage has real folders.
misconceptions.reality: No. Folders are just parts of the blob name, unless hierarchical namespace is on.

misconceptions.myth: Any storage account can have NFS shares.
misconceptions.reality: No. NFS needs premium file shares.

comparisons.difference: An S3 bucket is like a container (but each bucket name is global). EFS (NFS) and FSx are like Azure file shares.

troubleshooting.symptom: The anonymous access options are greyed out.
troubleshooting.cause: The account has 'Allow blob anonymous access' turned off.
troubleshooting.fix: Turn it on for the account (if your rules allow it), or use a SAS or Entra ID.

troubleshooting.cause: The container is Private. Anonymous requests get 404, not 403.
troubleshooting.fix: Set the level to Blob, or use a SAS.

troubleshooting.symptom: You can't set a share's size limit above 5 TiB.
troubleshooting.cause: Large file shares isn't turned on.
troubleshooting.fix: Turn on large file shares. You can't turn it off again.

troubleshooting.symptom: Mounting an NFS share on Linux fails.
troubleshooting.cause: NFS needs a premium share and private network access, and has its own secure-transfer rules.
troubleshooting.fix: Use a FileStorage account with a private endpoint or service endpoint, and follow the NFS mounting steps.

configuration.limits: Container and share names: 3 to 63 characters
Standard share: 5 TiB, or 100 TiB with large file shares
configuration.permissions: Storage Blob Data Contributor (data) or Contributor (management), to create containers
Storage Account Contributor, to create file shares
configuration.prerequisites: A storage account of the right type
Anonymous access allowed on the account, for public containers
